messages:
Alex: Heads-up — customer acme-corp on dedicated pool dp-nyc-2 is reporting sustained throughput drop since 02:10 UTC, seeing lots of 429s and tiny batch sizes. linking quick logs + timeline. :eyes:
infra-bot: alert: dp-nyc-2 throughput anomaly detected (drop 34% p95 tokens/sec) at 3114500005
Maya: Which API errors exactly? 429 or upstream 502/504? Any auth/billing failures in the logs?
Alex: Primarily HTTP 429 rate_limited from the runtime, a few 500s when prefills backlog exploded. No 401s. Billing looked normal for that tenant, but quotas for dedicated pool were near cap. Snip of recent log lines:
```
[02:11:03] batcher: accepted_batch_size=2 total_tokens=66 max_batch_tokens=4096 fill_timeout_ms=20
[02:11:04] scheduler: queue_depth=720 prefills_inflight=18 continuous_mode=true
[02:11:05] runtime: HTTP 429 tenant=acme-corp pool=dp-nyc-2 route=/v1/generate
```

Ben: I pulled the console graph — p50 token latency up 2.1x, p95 up 3.7x. interestingly average batch size dropped from ~48 tokens to ~6 around the same time as an autoscale resize event at 02:09.
Kevin: autoscale resize? Did a node drain/replace run in dp-nyc-2? That can temporarily change packing behavior.
Alex: Yes, there was a scheduled resize to add capacity — but the autoscaler reverted after failing healthchecks. So capacity briefly changed and then we ended up with leftover small batchers.
Jordan (oncall): Jumping in. Steps I want to run: 1) repro locally with a small synthetic load to see batcher behavior, 2) check prefill and KV cache hits, 3) confirm scheduler quantum/fill_timeout values.
Maya: Repro curl (quick):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"open-quant", "input":"lot of short prompts", "max_tokens":16}'
```
Run 500 reqs/s for a minute, watch batch sizes in logs.
Ben: On repro I see continuous_batcher stuck with many tiny windows: fill_timeout_ms=20 + max_batch_tokens computed per request smaller due to token_estimates coming back wrong for some tenants. There is an edge where token_estimate heuristic returns 1 for many prompts and packer refuses to colocate longer requests -> fragmentation.
Alex: Also found this in support logs: when autoscale partially failed, the scheduler started conservative packing (quantum drop from 8ms -> 2ms) which reduced coalescing.
Kevin: Potential quick mitigations: raise fill_timeout_ms to 40ms for dp-nyc-2, temporarily raise max_batch_tokens override to 8192, and enable lenient_prefill for that pool. Risks: slightly higher tail latency for some prompts but immediate throughput improvement.
Jordan (oncall): I'll run the config bump in canary on 2 nodes in dp-nyc-2 now. tagging SRE.
support-bot: support ticket #INC-2026 created for acme-corp, assigned to Ben. Link: https://support.redwood.local/INC-2026
Ben: After canary change: batch sizes increased from ~6 -> ~36 in 30s, 429 rate dropped to baseline. Observed minor p50 increase of 80ms. Looks good.
Maya: Next steps: 1) investigate token_estimate regression in the heuristic service, 2) add guard to avoid quantum dropping below 4ms during partial autoscale, 3) add ticket to autoscaler to avoid revert flaps triggering conservative packing.
Alex: Filed follow-ups: AUTOSCALE-423, TOKENEST-87, SCHED-319. Also notifying product for customer communication. :thumbsup:
Jordan (oncall): Closing oncall loop — will keep the canary config for 1h then roll if stable. If 429s reoccur, we revert.
Kevin: FYI — billing/auth checked: no 401s, no billing spikes. Confirmed quota bump not needed for now.
Alex: Adding reproduction notes to the support ticket with the curl snippet and expected log markers (`accepted_batch_size`, `fill_timeout_ms`, `continuous_mode=true`).
Ben: Good triage. We should also add a small metric: "batch_coalesce_rate" to detect tiny-batch regressions earlier.
Maya: Agree. I'll open SLO alert PR for coalesce rate threshold.
Alex: Thanks all — monitoring continues, keeping this thread updated. :white_check_mark:
